name: Peak Hour Payment Switch
tagline: Route heavy traffic surges dynamically under provider latency, outages, and finite capacity.
narrative:
It is Friday afternoon at YamusaPay—the busiest traffic window of the week. A heavy mix of consumer transfers, high-value business payouts, international remittances, and time-critical payroll transactions flows through the payment switch.

Under heavy volume, your low-cost provider suffers severe latency and intermittent failures, while a primary alternative experiences a sudden outage. Every payment routed consumes provider capacity for multiple ticks until settlement completes. Every decision directly shapes future queue depth, available capacity, and timeout risk.
objective: Process the peak surge with high completion, zero overload rejections, at most two timeouts, and a low penalty score.
learningObjective: Design a load-aware routing algorithm that balances immediate transaction requirements against future provider capacity and latency.
intelligenceExplanation:
You begin with an empty rule set. Evaluate every incoming payment against live provider health before deciding its destination.

Filter out offline or ineligible providers first. Dispatch urgent payroll, time-sensitive, and high-value payments to low-latency, highly reliable routes before capacity is exhausted. For flexible, routine transactions, optimize across fees, current latency, and free capacity.

When a provider fails, avoid resubmitting to the same failing route; retry only if sufficient deadline budget remains, or hold temporarily if a healthy route will open.
hint: Filter ineligible or offline routes first, protect urgent payroll and near-deadline payments next, and distribute flexible work across healthy capacity.
hints: Filter out offline or incompatible routes using canRouteA, canRouteB, and canRouteC before evaluating performance metrics.
Prioritize time-critical payments (isPayroll, isPriority, near-deadline) onto your fastest, most reliable healthy routes.
Route routine consumer payments using live latency, remaining capacity, and expected cost to prevent bottlenecks.
On retries, select a different eligible provider than the last attempted route, provided deadlineRemaining allows another attempt.
brief: Route payments through Friday afternoon peak traffic, degraded providers, and unexpected outages.
context: Heavy transaction volume fills provider capacity while latency spikes, outages strike without warning, and payment deadlines tick down.
